title: Microservices and DDD in Laravel: Architecture Patterns for 2026
meta_description: Master microservices and domain-driven design in Laravel for 2026. Learn DDD patterns, service communication, and when to split monoliths for real architectural gains.
excerpt: Microservices aren't the answer to every scaling problem—but when they are, Laravel's ecosystem handles them beautifully. This guide covers domain-driven design patterns in Laravel, service decomposition strategies, inter-service communication, and the honest trade-offs that most tutorials skip.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: 63% of microservices adoptions increase complexity without proportional gains. Challenge the microservices default. Preview: DDD principles, modular monolith, extraction playbook, inter-service comms.
content_structure.section_1: Monolith first: why premature decomposition is the #1 Laravel architecture mistake. When a monolith genuinely needs to be split (team autonomy, independent scaling, technology diversity).
content_structure.section_2: DDD fundamentals for Laravel: bounded contexts, aggregates, domain events, value objects, repositories. Mapping DDD concepts to Laravel service providers, Eloquent models, and event system.
content_structure.section_3: Modular monolith with nwidart/laravel-modules: domain-organized module structure, inter-module communication via events, module-level service providers, keeping modules independently testable.
content_structure.section_4: Service extraction playbook: identify seam (bounded context boundary), build anti-corruption layer, move to separate repo/deployment, establish API contract, migrate data, decommission original.
content_structure.section_5: Inter-service communication: synchronous REST (when strong consistency needed), asynchronous events via queues (RabbitMQ/SQS), event sourcing with Spatie for audit trails.
content_structure.conclusion: Architecture decision flowchart. CTA: Download the Laravel Domain Architecture Template.
content_structure.faq_section: Q1: Should I use DDD even for small Laravel apps? Q2: How do I share code between Laravel microservices? Q3: How does Laravel's event system fit into DDD? Q4: When is a modular monolith better than microservices?

title: Laravel Testing with Pest and Pint: Modern Developer Experience Guide
meta_description: Master Laravel testing with Pest and code style with Pint in 2026. Learn testing architecture, type coverage, and DX practices that top Laravel teams use to ship confidently.
excerpt: Pest has transformed how Laravel teams write tests—and combined with Pint for code style, the modern Laravel developer experience is the best PHP has ever offered. This guide covers Pest architecture patterns, test organization, type coverage, and the DX tooling stack that high-velocity teams rely on.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: Pest adoption doubled in 2 years. Define the modern Laravel DX stack. Preview: Pest patterns, advanced techniques, Pint, static analysis, CI/CD integration.
content_structure.section_1: Pest vs PHPUnit: expressive syntax comparison, describe/it blocks vs test functions, expectation API vs assertions, architecture tests, parallel testing. Migration guide from PHPUnit.
content_structure.section_2: Testing architecture: unit tests (pure PHP, no framework), feature tests (HTTP layer, Laravel testing helpers), integration tests (with real DB). File organization conventions.
content_structure.section_3: Advanced Pest: datasets (parametric testing), hooks (beforeEach/afterEach), shared datasets across test files, architecture tests (Pest Architecture plugin for dependency enforcement).
content_structure.section_4: Pint setup: configuration, rule presets (Laravel, PER, PSR-12), custom rules, pre-commit hook integration, CI enforcement. Running Pint in watch mode during development.
content_structure.section_5: Static analysis: PHPStan + Larastan setup, level progression strategy (start at 0, raise incrementally), CI integration, type coverage reporting, fixing common Laravel false positives.
content_structure.conclusion: Full DX tooling stack checklist. CTA: Download the Laravel Testing and DX Setup Script.
